newsitem.title: FRANCE: French parliament approves night police searches.
newsitem.headline: French parliament approves night police searches.

text.p: The French parliament approved on Thursday a draft law submitted by Justice Minister Jacques Toubon authorising police searches at night to fight terrorism. The existing law bars searches before 6 a.m.

Under the new law, night searches will be possible only under certain conditions, such as when a crime is under way, when police fear evidence may be lost or when a search would prevent a terrorist act like the bomb attack on a Paris underground train which killed four commuters on December 3.
Investigators believe the bombing was carried out by Islamic guerrillas angry over French backing for Algeria.
The National Assembly also amended a new law on immigration to allow police to fingerprint foreigners from outside the European Union asking to visit France.
The measure is aimed at preventing visitors from taking up permanent residence in France without the necessary papers.
